title: Add cross-tool composite-key conformance coverage
description:
Rationale:
shape and rvl both consume profile key lists, so correctness depends on shared tuple semantics even though their domain outcomes differ. A reusable conformance surface should prevent either tool from narrowing to the first component, flattening tuples with colliding sentinels, or drifting in per-component normalization.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Define the shared ordered-tuple rules: ASCII-trim each component, any empty component is incomplete, missing-token strings remain literal key bytes, equality and ordering are lexicographic over component byte strings.
- Add reusable fixtures or helpers covering repeated first components, reordered rows, duplicate full tuples, empty secondary components, non-UTF-8 bytes, and sentinel-collision tuples.
- Assert machine output exposes authoritative component arrays while joined labels remain display-only.
- Wire the conformance coverage into both shape and rvl consumers or document the minimal consumer integration contract.
- Bump the crate version if the reusable API changes.
close_reason: Added reusable and live cross-tool composite-key conformance coverage with version bump.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: Added spine-rules 0.2.0 composite-key conformance API and fixture corpus; executable assertions cover per-component ASCII trim, incomplete components, literal missing tokens, repeated first components, structural sentinel collisions, non-UTF-8, duplicate tuples, component order, and lexicographic ordering. Added authoritative JSON component-array/display-label assertions and a live shape+rvl pipeline across reorder/change, duplicate, and empty-secondary cases. Also fixed upstream child reaping in pipe_tools and made the existing rvl value assertion explicit. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -- -D warnings; cargo test (19 passed, 3 doctests ignored); git diff --check. UBS reviewed: findings are intentional assertion panics and caller-selected subprocesses in this test-infrastructure crate.

title: Consume cmdrvl/evidence-protocol for conformance over protocol objects; add cargo-deny boundary ban on evidence-machine
description:
DECISION (Zac, 2026-09-15; canon: cmdrvl-context docs/02-architecture/evidence-machine.md §2 "Protocol origination and boundary rules"): the Evidence Protocol wire types live in a dedicated PUBLIC package `cmdrvl/evidence-protocol`. spine-rules stays the conformance/rules layer — it CONSUMES evidence-protocol; it does not become the protocol package. operator.v0 stays here.

DELIVER:
1. Add `evidence-protocol` as a dependency once the crate exists (path dep during bootstrap, then crates.io/git tag). Do not copy or re-declare any *.v0 type here.
2. Conformance rules over protocol objects, only as consumers appear — first candidates: R-xxx inquiry.v0 validates against schema + refuses ambiguous universe/completion; receipt.v0 has all four axes populated (execution, domain_disposition, coverage, claim_state); plan.v0 hash equals blake3 of canonical JSON; answer.v0 coverage totals reconcile (total == sum of terminal states). Each rule cites the consuming code in evidence-machine (em-3h0 / em-13q / em-36x). No speculative rules (AGENTS anti-conformance-metastasis).
3. Dependency-boundary check: add `deny.toml` (cargo-deny) banning crate `evidence-machine` and any git source under `github.com/SaltIO/`; wire `cargo deny check bans sources` into CI. Provide the same snippet as a reusable rule/template so every public operator repo (canon, shape, rvl, fingerprint, profile, verify, benchmark, twinning, decoding, crucible) can adopt it; file follow-ups there only when they first depend on spine-rules ≥ this version.
4. README: one paragraph on the three-layer split (evidence-protocol = types; spine-rules = rules + operator.v0; evidence-machine = private runtime) with the one-way dependency diagram from canon.

ACCEPTANCE: `cargo deny check` green with the ban present and a negative test (a fixture Cargo.toml adding evidence-machine fails the check); at least one protocol conformance rule with a passing and a failing fixture; no *.v0 struct defined in this crate (grep test).

title: Resolve exit-code trinity (0/1/2) semantic overload for multi-band and expected-change tools
description:
## Background & Evidence
`spine-rules` currently bans any exit code outside `{0, 1, 2}` (`rules/exit-code-range.yml` and `assert_exit_codes_trinity`). While clean for binary predicates, it creates three real agent bugs:

1. **`assess` conflation:** `assess` has 4 decision bands (`PROCEED`, `PROCEED_WITH_RISK`, `ESCALATE`, `BLOCK`) plus `REFUSAL` and CLI syntax errors. Packing these into `{0, 1, 2}` forces valid `BLOCK` policy verdicts into exit `2` alongside `REFUSAL` and CLI errors — an agent scripting `case $?` cannot tell a typo from a valid `BLOCK`.
2. **`rvl` vs `shape` under `set -e`:** `shape` exit `1` means halt (`INCOMPATIBLE`), whereas `rvl` exit `1` means normal expected `REAL_CHANGE` (aborting `set -e` bash scripts unless explicitly guarded, as `receipts-csv/SKILL.md` had to warn).
3. **`verify witness query`:** Exiting `1` on zero matches conflates "ran fine, empty result set" with domain `FAIL`.

## Goal
Define and enforce an explicit, backward-aware exit-code contract in `spine-rules`:
- Keep `0/1/2` for binary domain predicates (`shape`, `verify run`, `lock`, `hashbytes`, `fingerprint`, `pack verify`), while explicitly permitting a documented extended dictionary (e.g. `3` for valid `BLOCK` or separating `REFUSAL`/CLI error cleanly in `assess`) OR documenting the exact contract and deprecation migration in `operator.json`.
- Enforce the universal rule: read/query subcommands (`witness query`, `list`, `inspect`) NEVER exit `1` for empty results (`0` with `[]`).
- Document standard guidance for `--exit-zero-on-change` (or equivalent opt-in) on diff-style tools in `set -e` pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Updated exit-code ADR, ast-grep rule, and spine-rules assertions cleanly separating policy BLOCK from REFUSAL/CLI errors and banning exit-1 on empty query results.
close_reason: Verified by independent verifier at 4e24040: exit_codes 18 passed. ADR docs/exit-codes.md now has a concrete assess band table (PROCEED 0, PROCEED_WITH_RISK 0, ESCALATE 1 negative, BLOCK 3 policy, REFUSAL/CLI 2) accepted by assess_band_table_is_accepted via assert_exit_codes_trinity; doctor exempt from verdict domain; empty-query check asserts exactly [] with should_panic negatives (empty object, rows, exit 1, no JSON) and ADR says verify must opt in via fixture_empty_query_args; policy band 3 / expected_change opt-in coherent with bd-yes. Gate got stricter, no removed assertions beyond signature updates. NOT verified: ast-grep rules, real tool binaries; residual ambiguity: exit 1 is overloaded (ESCALATE/REAL_CHANGE/FAIL/doctor-unhealthy) and only documented by convention per tool; tests/pipeline.rs not re-run.

title: spine-rules v2: unify cross-tool family contract across all data and boundary CLIs
description:
## Background & Rationale
Individual `cmdrvl` spine tools have strong single-repo engineering (`operator.json`, `--describe`, `--schema`, refusal envelopes, Pass-1 `agent_ergonomics_audit`), yet cross-repo inspection revealed significant **family-level drift**:

- `benchmark`, `assess`, `veil`, `airlock`, and `decoding` are not yet wired into `spine-rules`.
- Tools expose 4 overlapping discovery surfaces (`--describe`, `--schema`, `capabilities --json`, `doctor capabilities --json` / `--robot-triage`) with divergent JSON schemas.
- `doctor` unhealthy exit codes disagree (`1` in `shape`/`canon` vs `2` in `verify`).
- Exit-code trinity (`0/1/2`) is overloaded in `assess` (`BLOCK` conflated with `REFUSAL`/CLI error in exit `2`) and `rvl` (`REAL_CHANGE` exits `1`, breaking `set -e` pipelines).
- Flag names drift across siblings (`--out` vs `--output`, `--capsule-dir` vs `--capsule-out`, `--json` vs `--emit json` vs `--render summary`).
- `NO_COLOR`/`TERM=dumb`/`isatty` and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` are inconsistently honored.

## Goal
Upgrade `spine-rules` into the single enforced family contract (`spine-rules` v2) so every data and boundary tool in `cmdrvl` feels like one coherent instrument to an AI agent.

## Verification
- Expand `golden_rules_suite!` and add cross-binary family conformance tests checking exit codes, doctor/capabilities schemas, flag conventions, and non-TTY/NO_COLOR discipline across all binaries.
acceptance_criteria: spine-rules v2 defines and enforces unified discovery, doctor, exit-code, flag, and env-discipline contracts across all core data and boundary tools.

title: Design shared cmdrvl-tabular crate (CSV, TSV, JSONL, Parquet, XLSX) for spine format parity
description:
## Background & Evidence
Format support across the data spine is currently fragmented, breaking real-world agent workflows:
- `fingerprint`: `csv, xlsx, pdf, html, markdown, text` (`calamine` + `csv` + `lopdf`)
- `profile`, `shape`, `rvl`: **CSV only** (`rvl` only uses `polars`/`arrow` in dev-dependencies for benchmarks)
- `canon`: `csv, tsv, jsonl, ndjson` (no Parquet, no XLSX)
- `verify`, `benchmark`: `csv, json, jsonl, parquet` via bundled DuckDB (no XLSX)

Agents working in analytics (Parquet/JSONL) cannot run `shape` or `rvl`. Agents working in finance/ops (Excel `.xlsx` loan tapes, Argus models, rent rolls) cannot pass `.xlsx` sheets into `shape`, `rvl`, `profile`, `verify`, `canon`, or `benchmark`.

## Goal
Design a lightweight, deterministic shared Rust crate (`cmdrvl-tabular` — either as a workspace member or dedicated `cmdrvl/tabular` repo referenced by `spine-rules` conformance) that provides a single uniform tabular reader interface across:
- CSV / TSV (with existing auto-dialect detection + `profile slice` preamble handling)
- JSONL / NDJSON
- Parquet (lightweight `parquet`/`arrow` reader without pulling full DuckDB into every binary)
- Excel `.xlsx` / `.xls` (via `calamine`, with explicit `--sheet <name|index>` selection and deterministic `E_AMBIGUOUS_SHEET` refusal when multi-sheet workbooks omit `--sheet`)

## Deliverables
- Design spec & trait API preserving `spine-rules` composite-key ordered-tuple byte semantics (`NA`/`NULL` literal key handling, deterministic type classification, streaming/memory bounds `--max-rows`/`--max-bytes`).
- Cross-format golden conformance fixtures proving identical results whether a dataset is supplied as CSV, Parquet, JSONL, or XLSX.
acceptance_criteria: Published design spec + crate skeleton/conformance test plan for cmdrvl-tabular covering CSV, TSV, JSONL, Parquet, and XLSX with deterministic sheet selection and composite-key parity.
close_reason: Verified and published. (1) Independent verifier at tabular 704918e: cargo test 44 passed 0 ignored, real fixtures of all five formats (PAR1, PK zip, CDFV2 encrypted, text, jsonl) compared to a hard-coded golden grid, composite-key parity via reference_key_tuple and assert_ordered_tuple_semantics, planted negatives gave typed refusals with no cell content (E_AMBIGUOUS_SHEET, E_UNSUPPORTED_VALUE decimal/timestamp, E_TOO_LARGE at the exact max_rows boundary), design doc matches the code. (2) Orchestrator at 484e3c9 from a FRESH CLONE of github.com/cmdrvl/tabular with the pinned spine-rules git dependency: cargo test --locked = unit 3 + conformance 9 + refusals 32 = 44 passed, no #[ignore]; tracked-text scan clean (no bead IDs, private paths or internal names); LICENSE identical to spine-rules; README honest (pre-1.0, publish=false, API may change). (3) cmdrvl/tabular made PUBLIC by operator decision; anonymous https ls-remote returns 484e3c9. Acceptance 'published design spec + crate skeleton/conformance test plan covering CSV, TSV, JSONL, Parquet, XLSX with deterministic sheet selection and composite-key parity': met. NOT done and documented as v0 limits: true streaming (open() materializes; max_rows/max_bytes bound cost only), v1 temporal/decimal types (Parquet decimal/date/timestamp and XLSX datetime are refused), CSV dialect detector not yet checked against shape's, fingerprint pins calamine =0.26.1 vs tabular 0.38, no zip-bomb guard, .xls/.xlsm untested; these are tracked in the follow-up bead for v1 and are out of scope of the design+skeleton acceptance.

title: Codify blake3-first canonical hashing policy and shared lock.v0 dual-algorithm verifier
description:
## Evidence (Cross-Repo Audit)
Lockfile verification has drifted across the spine:
- `hashbytes` / `lock` emit `lock.v0` with `bytes_hash` prefixed by `blake3:` or `sha256:`.
- `benchmark/src/lock_check.rs` parses `lock.v0` `bytes_hash` but hardcodes `Sha256` (fails on `blake3:`).
- `verify/crates/verify-duckdb/src/lock_check.rs` hardcodes `lock.input.v1`, `content_hash`, and `sha256:` only.

## Scope
1. Document the canonical hashing policy: `blake3:` is canonical internally across the spine, while `sha256:` is supported for external/legacy interoperability.
2. Provide a reusable `lock.v0` verification helper and golden conformance fixtures (both `blake3:` and `sha256:` pass/drift/unknown-algo cases) in `spine-rules` so downstream tools (`verify`, `benchmark`, `rvl`, `shape`, `profile`, `pack`) share one contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical hashing policy (`blake3:` internal default, `sha256:` interop) documented in `spine-rules`.
- Shared `lock.v0` verification helper & conformance fixtures test both `blake3:` and `sha256:` pass/mismatch/unknown-prefix paths.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
Implemented+verified in spine-rules commit 59ebbd1d62b8940f9610096fc7b5bc746e6ca9b4 (pushed to origin/main right after this comment). Checked lock state first: lock bd-16f is CLOSED (verified by orchestrator); lock bd-rpf is IN_PROGRESS (Lane C, implemented d4d06d8, not closed). I did not touch the lock repo; this change is only in spine-rules and does not depend on bd-rpf.
Policy (docs/hashing-policy.md): blake3: canonical inside the spine, sha256: supported for external/legacy interop; prefix names the algorithm; verification uses the algorithm the lock names (never the tool's favourite); unknown prefix refused, never guessed; hashes are over raw bytes.
Shared verifier (src/lockfile.rs, pub mod lockfile; new dependencies blake3 1.8 and sha2 0.10): parse() (lock.v0 only), candidates() (exact path, else unique basename, ambiguous matches nothing), verify_member() -> Verified/Drift/NotLocked or typed LockRefusal (UnknownAlgorithm, Malformed, UnsupportedVersion), HashAlgorithm. Conformance: conformance_cases() + run_conformance(check) + reference_check(); fixtures are REAL output of 'vacuum data --no-witness | hashbytes --algorithm <alg> --no-witness | lock --no-witness --dataset-id t --output <alg>.lock.json' (lock 0.6.0, hashbytes/vacuum 0.5.0) over fixtures/lock_v0/loans.csv. Cases for BOTH algorithms: matching bytes verify, one changed byte is drift, two members with one basename are NotLocked; plus not-locked input, unknown algorithm prefix (md5:), member without bytes_hash, unknown version (lock.v9) refused.
Planted negatives (tests/lockfile.rs, 7 tests): a sha256-only verifier (the benchmark drift) FAILS conformance on the blake3 cases and passes the sha256 ones; a verifier that guesses ambiguous basenames FAILS; the reference passes every case; drift reports the lock's own prefix on both sides; refusals are typed.

title: Unify operator.json (--describe) and capabilities --json into a single canonical family contract
description:
## Background & Evidence
Currently agents encounter four overlapping discovery surfaces on spine tools:
1. `<tool> --describe` (`operator.v0`)
2. `<tool> --schema` (output JSON Schema)
3. `<tool> capabilities --json` (top-level)
4. `<tool> doctor capabilities --json` / `--robot-triage`

Moreover, `verify` emits `verify.capabilities.v1` at top level and `verify.doctor.capabilities.v1` under `doctor`, `shape`/`rvl`/`fingerprint` use `<tool>.doctor.v1`, `airlock`'s `operator.json` omits `schema_version`/`exit_codes`/`refusals`/`invocation`, and `benchmark`/`veil`/`decoding` lack `operator.json` altogether.

## Goal
Define a single canonical machine-readable contract in `spine-rules` (e.g., `operator.v1` / unified `capabilities --json` envelope) where:
- One shared Rust struct + JSON Schema backs both `operator.json` (`--describe`) and `capabilities --json` (no dual maintenance or drift).
- Every tool declares `tool_version`, `contract_version`, `commands`, `exit_codes`, `refusals`/`error_kinds`, `env_vars`, `formats`, `side_effects`, and `pipeline` adjacency.
- `golden_rules_suite!` asserts that `Cargo.toml` package version == `operator.json` version (catching drift like `shape` 0.9.0 vs 0.8.0) and that `operator.json` subcommands include `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, and `doctor` (catching omissions like `vacuum`).
acceptance_criteria: spine-rules publishes unified operator/capabilities serde types + JSON Schema + golden_rules_suite! version-parity and subcommand-parity assertions with unit tests.
close_reason: Re-closed after the reopen fix. Verified by independent verifier at origin/main c9da564 (includes 5ec6622) from a git-archive extract: helpers now dispatch on schema_version via manifest_view (src/helpers.rs:21-86): operator.v1 -> strict OperatorContract::parse, operator.v0 -> legacy types, anything else panics; serde aliases removed from src/contract.rs so a legacy-spelling file declaring operator.v1 fails with 'missing field tool_version'; tests/manifest_helpers.rs 6 passed (real v1 manifest passes trinity + refusal collection, legacy-spelling-claiming-v1 fails, v0 still works, unknown schema rejected, empty refusals legal, non-E_ refusal rejected); docs/exit-codes.md has the no-verdict/no-refusal-envelope rule (veil); contract 16, exit_codes 18, manifest_helpers 6 passed; no #[ignore], no severity downgrades, one test replaced by a stricter one. Real-world check on committed manifests: veil operator.v1 PASSES validate() and the helpers; rvl FAILS (declares operator.v1 but still uses legacy 'version': correct rejection, rvl must migrate: tracked in rvl bd-59w verification); assess origin/main manifest is v0 (passes via the v0 path, strict parse fails until bd-wtu migrates it). NOT verified: macro-expanded generated tests in a real consumer crate (veil bd-bf2 and assess bd-wtu are the consumers; assess owes the bad-manifest demonstration); family suite ran 22 of 23 on a machine at load ~250 and 100% disk (bare_invocation_that_exits_passes timed out at 10s, passed alone: environmental, not re-run quietly); smoke/pipeline/composite_key; clippy/fmt/ubs.

title: cmdrvl-tabular: add open_bytes() in-memory API and wasm32-unknown-unknown compile check
description:
## Context
`cmdrvl/tabular` already isolates its only C dependency (`zstd-sys`) behind an optional `zstd` Cargo feature (`Cargo.toml:10-13`), making it almost ready for pure-Rust `wasm32-unknown-unknown` browser execution (e.g., zero-upload client-side CSV/XLSX/Parquet diffs and offline pack verification).

## Current Blocker
- `src/lib.rs:186` only exposes `open(path: &Path, opts: &OpenOptions)` calling `std::fs::metadata(path)` and passing `&Path` to `csv_reader`, `jsonl_reader`, `parquet_reader`, and `xlsx_reader`.

## Scope
1. Add `pub fn open_bytes(bytes: Vec<u8>, name_hint: Option<&str>, opts: &OpenOptions) -> Result<Table, Refusal>` (using `Cursor<Vec<u8>>` / `bytes::Bytes` internally across CSV, TSV, JSONL, Parquet, and XLSX, honoring `max_bytes`, `max_rows`, and `max_uncompressed_bytes`).
2. Keep `open(path: &Path, ...)` unchanged for streaming disk reads.
3. Add a `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features` check in `cmdrvl/tabular` CI and parity tests proving `open_bytes` yields byte-identical headers/cells/refusals to `open`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cmdrvl_tabular::open_bytes` supports CSV, TSV, JSONL, Parquet, and XLSX with identical headers, cells, and refusals to `open`.
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features` passes cleanly in CI.
- Zero native streaming regression in `open(path)`.

title: cmdrvl-tabular v1: temporal and decimal types, true streaming, zip-bomb guard, dialect parity with shape
description: Follow-up to bd-e0g (closed). The v0 skeleton lives at https://github.com/cmdrvl/tabular (public). v0 limits that block Wave 3 adoption by typed-data tools: (1) Parquet decimal/date/timestamp/binary/float16/nested and XLSX datetime/duration/error cells are REFUSED, which blocks verify, benchmark and canon on loan tapes and rent rolls; define the v1 canonical rendering for each and add conformance fixtures; (2) open() materializes the whole table, so memory is O(table) and XLSX O(sheet): add a real streaming iterator (rows() currently never yields Err); (3) no zip-bomb guard on XLSX (max_bytes checks compressed size only); (4) CSV dialect detector is a re-implementation from shape's source and has two documented scoring quirks: run it against shape's own fixtures and reconcile before shape adopts it (shape bd-o7y2); (5) fingerprint pins calamine =0.26.1 while tabular uses 0.38: prove fingerprint's code compiles on 0.38 before fingerprint adopts it (fingerprint bd-jxd); (6) .xls/.xlsm, XLSX formulas and merged cells, backslash-escaped CSV and Parquet brotli have no fixtures. Not blocking the Wave 3 first tier (shape, rvl, profile, fingerprint on CSV/TSV/JSONL and v0 types).

title: Add assert_no_raw_cell_leak zero-retention helper to golden_rules_suite!
description:
## Evidence (Cross-Repo Audit)
Source audits caught raw cell-value leaks in default output across `verify`, `benchmark`, and `shape` (`bd-pitd`). Any tool authorized to run on sensitive inputs under `veil` must enforce default redaction mechanically rather than by convention.

## Scope
1. Add an opt-in/standard `assert_no_raw_cell_leak` helper in `spine-rules` (wired into `golden_rules_suite!` for data/analysis tools).
2. The helper runs the tool against canary-seeded fixture inputs WITHOUT `--explicit` and asserts that none of the canary values (or sensitive column-name leaks in free-text reasons) appear in stdout or stderr.
3. Verify that tools supporting `--explicit` declare it consistently in `operator.v1` metadata so `veil` can enforce flag bans uniformly.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spine-rules` exposes `assert_no_raw_cell_leak` with unit tests proving it catches both stdout and stderr canary leaks.
- Documented in `spine-rules` conformance guide for all `veil`-authorized tools.

title: Standardize doctor JSON schemas, unhealthy exit codes, flag aliases, and NO_COLOR/SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH rules
description:
## Background & Evidence
Cross-repo inspection of `src/doctor.rs` and CLI parsers across all 14 tools showed:
- **Doctor schema split:** `fingerprint`/`shape`/`rvl` use single schema `<tool>.doctor.v1`; `vacuum`/`lock`/`pack`/`verify`/`assess`/`canon`/`benchmark`/`airlock`/`decoding` use three (`*.doctor.{health,capabilities,triage}.v1`).
- **Doctor exit-code split:** Unhealthy doctor checks exit `1` in `shape`/`canon`, but `2` in `verify` (`crates/verify-cli/src/doctor.rs:106`).
- **Flag drift:** `--out` (`profile`, `verify`, `fingerprint`, `airlock`) vs `--output` (`pack`, `decoding`, `canon registry build`); `--capsule-dir` (`shape`) vs `--capsule-out` (`rvl`); `--json` vs `--emit json` (`canon`).
- **Env conventions:** None of the core binaries check `NO_COLOR`/`TERM=dumb`/`isatty`; only `pack` honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.

## Goal
Encode canonical family standards in `spine-rules` + `golden_rules_suite!`:
- One shared `cmdrvl.doctor.v1` payload contract (`health`, `capabilities`, `triage`) and one deterministic unhealthy exit code (`1` = findings/unhealthy, `2` = CLI/usage error) across all tools.
- Canonical flag dictionary (`--out` with `--output` alias where legacy exists, `--capsule-dir`, `--json`, `--explicit`, `--no-witness`).
- Reusable `golden_rules_suite!` assertions for `NO_COLOR=1` / non-TTY ANSI-free stdout, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` determinism on timestamped artifacts, and bare-invocation non-hang check (stdin=`/dev/null`, stdout piped).
acceptance_criteria: spine-rules enforces unified doctor schema/exit code (1 for findings), canonical flag lint checks, NO_COLOR/non-TTY ANSI check, and bare-invocation non-hang test.
close_reason: Verified by independent verifier at 4e24040: family 23 passed. cmdrvl.doctor.v1 JSON Schema + doctor_schema_matches_struct (required keys derived by deleting keys from a real report) + doctor_schema_and_validate_agree (4 accept/6 reject); contract==capabilities equality check with negatives incl should_panic against real sh script; exit-1 resolved: tools with doctor must declare 1, new 'unhealthy' domain valid only on code 1, stale exit_codes.rs comment fixed, docs say --exit-zero-on-change affects verdict only; README 'Migrating from today's spellings' keeps --robot-triage etc as aliases for >=1 release. Earlier real negatives retained (exit-2 doctor, bare invocation hang, forced color, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH ignored). No gate weakening. NOT verified: aliases are documented not test-enforced; --out/--capsule-dir at binary level; doctor schema lacks additionalProperties:false.
